title: The Harmony of Instruction — Treasure, Trust and Watchfulness
content:
Treasure, Trust and Watchfulness

Read Instructions · Instructions index · Beyond the Torah · Counting and classification guide

This Harmony follows themes through Christ, the apostles, parables, wisdom and the prophets. Open the complementary Christ-study collection. The two views serve different purposes; their entry counts are not added together.

The Harmony of Instruction · His own commandments: in the world · Christ, the apostles, the parables, Proverbs and the Psalms

← Prayer, Fasting and Giving · The Harmony of Instruction: all subjects · The Church and Its Mission →

Possessions, anxiety, fear, false teachers, and readiness for His coming.

Each section follows one order: the word of Christ; the apostles who hand it on; the parables; the wisdom of Proverbs; the Psalms; and the Law, the Prophets and the rest of Scripture. Verses of Proverbs and the Psalms are quoted in full from the Saints Translation; everything else is linked to the place where it is given in full. Psalms are numbered as in the Greek, with the Hebrew number in parentheses. The selection is an editor’s gathering: a doorway into the text, not an addition to it.

On this page: Treasure · Trust · Watchfulness

Treasure

Treasure on earth is kept in a pierced bag, says Haggai; the one who stores it does not know for whom he gathers, says the psalm. The Lord says where to keep it instead, and whose image is on the coin and whose on the man.

The word of Christ

74. Not to store up treasures on earth, but in heaven. Matthew 6:19–21

Do not store up treasures for yourselves upon earth, where moth and consumption destroy and where thieves break through and steal. But store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither moth nor consumption destroys and where thieves neither break through nor steal. For where your treasure is, there your heart will also be.

Matthew 6:19–21

75. You cannot serve God and mammon. Matthew 6:24

No one can serve as a slave to two masters: for he will either hate the one and love the other, or hold to one and despise the other. You cannot serve as a slave to God and mammon.

Matthew 6:24

76. To guard against all greed, for life is not in the abundance of possessions. Luke 12:15

77. To make friends by means of unrighteous mammon; to be faithful in very little. Luke 16:9–10

78. To give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s. Matthew 22:21

The apostles hand it on

43. Godliness with contentment is great gain; the love of money is a root of all evils. 1 Timothy 6:6–10

But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into the world, because neither can we carry anything out. But having food and coverings, with these we will be content. But those who want to become rich fall into temptation and a snare and many foolish and harmful desires, which plunge human beings into ruin and destruction. For the love of money is a root of all evils, and some, reaching for it, wandered from the faith and pierced themselves with many pains.

1 Timothy 6:6–10

44. The rich are not to set their hope on uncertain riches but to be rich in good works, storing up a good foundation for the future. 1 Timothy 6:17–19

45. Come now, you rich: your gold and silver have rusted; the wages you withheld from the workers cry out. James 5:1–5

50. To be subject to the governing authorities and to pay to all what is owed: tax to whom tax, honor to whom honor. Romans 13:1 · Romans 13:6–7

51. We must obey God rather than human beings. Acts 5:29

66. Not to love the world or the things in the world. 1 John 2:15–17

123. Let marriage be held in honor; be content with what you have, for He has said, I will never leave you. Hebrews 13:4–6

In parable

The Rich Fool. So is the one who stores up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.

The Shrewd Steward. The sons of this age are more prudent toward their own generation than the sons of light.

The Rich Man and Lazarus. If they do not hear Moses and the Prophets, neither will they be persuaded if someone rises from the dead.

The wisdom of Proverbs

Better a small portion with the fear of the Lord
than great storehouses with fearlessness.

Proverbs 15:16

A good name is more desirable than much wealth,
and good favor is above silver and gold.
Rich and poor met one another,
and the Lord made both.

Proverbs 22:1–2

There are those who make themselves rich while having nothing,
and those who humble themselves amid much wealth.

Proverbs 13:7

Fear God, son, and the king,
and disobey neither of them;

Proverbs 24:21

In the Psalms

Indeed a person passes through as an image;
yet they are troubled in vain.
He stores treasure and does not know for whom he will gather it.

Psalm 38 (39):7

Better is a little for the righteous
than the great wealth of sinners.

Psalm 36 (37):16

Do not hope in injustice or long for plunder;
if wealth flows, do not attach your heart.

Psalm 61 (62):11

The Law, the Prophets and the rest of Scripture

In the commandments of the Law: 476. Not to covet

Made according to the image of God Genesis 1:27
He gives you strength to produce wealth Deuteronomy 8:17–18
Everything is Yours 1 Chronicles 29:14
Naked I came, naked I depart Job 1:21
He will take nothing from his toil Ecclesiastes 5:12–14
Let the rich not boast in his wealth Jeremiah 9:22–23
Seek the peace of the land Jeremiah 36:7
A God in the heavens whom we fear Daniel 3:16–18
Wages into a pierced bundle Haggai 1:6

Trust

Do not be anxious; do not fear. He points to the ravens, which the Psalms and Job had already seen fed by God, and which fed Elijah. Cast your care upon the Lord, and He will nourish you.

The word of Christ

79. Not to be anxious for your life, what you will eat or wear. Matthew 6:25–26

Therefore I tell you: do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear. Is life not more than food, and the body more than clothing? Look at the birds of the sky: they do not sow or reap or gather into storehouses, yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth more than they?

Matthew 6:25–26

80. Not to fear those who kill the body; to fear Him who can destroy both soul and body. Matthew 10:28

81. Not to let your heart be troubled; to believe in God and in Him. John 14:1

82. To take courage: He has overcome the world. John 16:33

The apostles hand it on

38. Not to be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and petition with thanksgiving to make your requests known to God. Philippians 4:6–7

Be anxious about nothing, but in everything, by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses every understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.

Philippians 4:6–7

39. To cast all your anxiety upon Him, because He cares for you. 1 Peter 5:7

51. We must obey God rather than human beings. Acts 5:29

In parable

The Seed Growing of Itself. The kingdom grows as seed does, night and day, the sower knows not how, until the harvest.

The wisdom of Proverbs

You will not fear an approaching fright or the oncoming assaults of the ungodly,
for the Lord will be upon all your ways and support your foot so that you are not shaken.

Proverbs 3:25–26

having feared and felt shame before people, they were tripped up;
but one who trusts in the Lord will rejoice.
Impiety gives a man a fall;
but one who trusts in the Master will be saved.

Proverbs 29:25

The Lord will not starve a righteous life,
but He will overturn the life of the impious.

Proverbs 10:3

In the fear of the Lord is hope of strength,
and he leaves a support for his children.

Proverbs 14:26

In the Psalms

Cast your care upon the Lord, and He will nourish you;
He will never give the righteous a shaking.

Psalm 54 (55):23

I was young and indeed have grown old,
and I have not seen a righteous person abandoned
or his offspring seeking loaves.

Psalm 36 (37):25

By day I will fear,
but I will hope in You.
In God I will praise my words all day.
In God I have hoped; I will not fear.
What will flesh do to me?

Psalm 55 (56):4–5

who gives the cattle their food
and to the young ravens who call upon Him.

Psalm 146 (147):9

The Lord is my illumination and my Savior; whom will I fear?
The Lord is the protector of my life; of whom will I be afraid?

Psalm 26 (27):1

The Law, the Prophets and the rest of Scripture

In the commandments of the Law: 5. To fear Him

The Lord will fight for you Exodus 14:13–14
Be strong and courageous Joshua 1:9
The ravens feed Elijah 1 Kings 17:4–6
Those with us are more 2 Kings 6:16
Who prepared food for a raven? Job 38:41
Do not fear its fear Isaiah 8:12–13
Do not fear, for I am with you Isaiah 41:10
Whom did you dread? A mortal Isaiah 51:12–13
Though the fig tree bears no fruit Habakkuk 3:17–18

Watchfulness

Stay awake. The prophets stood at their watch, and they warned of prophets who speak from their own heart and of watchmen who love to doze. Wisdom blesses the one who keeps awake at her doors day by day, and the psalmist waits for the Lord from the morning watch until night.

The word of Christ

83. To stay awake, for you do not know the day or the hour. Matthew 25:13

Therefore keep watch, because you know neither the day nor the hour.

Matthew 25:13

84. To watch yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down, and to stay awake at all times, praying. Luke 21:34–36

85. To beware of false prophets, who come in sheep’s clothing. Matthew 7:15–16

Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves. You will recognize them by their fruits. Do people gather grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?

Matthew 7:15–16

86. To beware of the leaven of the Pharisees. Matthew 16:6

87. Not to give what is holy to dogs or cast your pearls before swine. Matthew 7:6

88. To be prudent as snakes and innocent as doves. Matthew 10:16

89. To remember Lot’s wife. Luke 17:32–33

90. To acknowledge Him before people. Matthew 10:32–33

The apostles hand it on

4. To believe in the Lord Jesus; to confess with the mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in the heart that God raised Him. Romans 10:9–10

Because if you confess Jesus as Lord with your mouth, and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved; for with the heart one believes for righteousness, and with the mouth one confesses for salvation.

Romans 10:9–10

34. Blessing and cursing come out of the same mouth; this ought not to be. Can a fig tree bear olives?. James 3:9–12

56. If we endure, we shall also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He also will deny us. 2 Timothy 2:11–13

57. The day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night; so let us not sleep as the rest do, but stay awake and be sober. 1 Thessalonians 5:1–6

59. The day of the Lord will come like a thief; what sort of people ought you to be, in holy conduct and godliness. 2 Peter 3:10–12

60. To be patient until the coming of the Lord; the Judge is standing at the doors. James 5:7–9

61. Not to believe every spirit, but to test the spirits, because many false prophets have gone out into the world. 1 John 4:1–3

62. Savage wolves will come in among you, not sparing the flock; therefore be alert. Acts 20:29–31

91. These things happened as examples for us: not to be idolaters, not to commit sexual immorality, not to test Christ, not to grumble. 1 Corinthians 10:1–11

96. Sodom and Gomorrah were condemned to ruin as an example, and righteous Lot was rescued. 2 Peter 2:6–9

97. In the days of Noah eight souls were saved through water, which corresponds to baptism that now saves you. 1 Peter 3:20–21

120. With the Lord one day is as a thousand years: He is patient, not wishing any to perish. 2 Peter 3:8–9

In parable

The Ten Virgins. Five were prudent and took oil; the bridegroom came, and the door was shut.

The Doorkeeper. Stay awake, for you do not know when the master of the house is coming.

The Watchful Slaves. Blessed are those slaves whom the master finds awake: he will gird himself and serve them.

The Thief in the Night. If the householder had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake.

The Faithful and the Wicked Slave. Blessed is the slave whom his master finds so doing when he comes.

The Talents. To each according to his ability; to everyone who has, more will be given.

The Minas. Do business until I come.

The Budding Fig Tree. When its branch becomes tender, you know that summer is near.

The Weeds among the Wheat. Good seed and darnel, the weed an enemy sowed, grow together until the harvest, when the Son of Man sends His angels to separate them. The Lord explains it Himself.

The Dragnet. The net gathers every kind; at the end of the age the angels separate the evil from the righteous.

The Blind Leading the Blind. Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?

The wisdom of Proverbs

How long do you lie down, sluggard?
When will you rise from sleep?
You sleep a little, sit a little, doze a little,
and clasp your chest with your hands a little;
then poverty arrives beside you like an evil traveler,
and want like a good runner.

Proverbs 6:9–11

Happy is the man who will listen to me,
and the person who will keep my ways,
staying awake at my doors day by day,
guarding the posts of my entrances.

Proverbs 8:34

Do not boast of things for tomorrow,
for you do not know what the coming day will bear.

Proverbs 27:1

The innocent person believes every word,
but the resourceful comes to reconsideration.

Proverbs 14:15

In the Psalms

Because of Your law I waited for You, Lord;
my soul waited for Your word.
My soul hoped in the Lord
from the morning watch until night;
from the morning watch let Israel hope in the Lord.

Psalm 129 (130):5–6

Unless the Lord builds a house,
those building it have labored in vain.
Unless the Lord guards a city,
the watchman has kept awake in vain.

Psalm 126 (127):1

My eyes were awake before dawn
to meditate on Your sayings.

Psalm 118 (119):148

And I spoke of Your testimonies
before kings, and I was not ashamed.

Psalm 118 (119):46

I proclaimed good news of righteousness in a great assembly;
look, I will certainly not restrain my lips;
Lord, You know.
I did not hide Your righteousness in my heart;
I spoke of Your truth and Your salvation.
I did not hide Your mercy and Your truth from a great congregation.

Psalm 39 (40):10–11

The Law, the Prophets and the rest of Scripture

In the commandments of the Law: 43. Not to listen to a prophet who calls you after other gods · 6. To sanctify His Name · 7. Not to profane His Name

The serpent, most shrewd Genesis 3:1
Noah enters the ark Genesis 7:1
Do not look back Genesis 19:17
Lot’s wife Genesis 19:26
The prophet who speaks what I did not order Deuteronomy 18:20–22
I sleep, but my heart keeps watch Song of Songs 5:2
Watchmen who love to doze Isaiah 56:10
They speak from their own heart Jeremiah 23:16–17
A watchman for Israel Ezekiel 33:6–7
Those inscribed in the book Daniel 12:1–3
The Lord’s day is near Joel 2:1
Prophets who lead My people astray Micah 3:5
I will stand at my watch Habakkuk 2:1–3
Near and very swift Zephaniah 1:14
The day coming, burning like an oven Malachi 3:19
